To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of cancer vaccines and monoclonal antibodies can be used for the immunotherapy of cancer.

(1) combination immunotherapy with cancer vaccine and mAb can synergistically enhance immunity against tumors; (2) the combination of cancer vaccine and mAbs can be used to treat cancer patients with minimal toxicity; and (3) the combination immunotherapy can be used to induce long-lasting antitumor immunity.

the use of cancer vaccines in combination with mAbs that target costimulatory or coinhibitory molecules can lead to enhanced antitumor immunity and that the combination of cancer vaccines with mAbs that block the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway is particularly promising.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel immunotherapeutic approaches to treat cancer, including the development of vaccines and immunostimulatory mAbs for cancer treatment.
the discovery of new cancer vaccines and the development of new therapeutic combinations for the treatment of patients with cancer.
the design, production, and characterization of vaccines and mAbs that are intended to treat cancer and infectious diseases, and to enhance the immune response to infectious agents and tumors.

the combination of immunostimulatory monoclonal antibodies with tumor vaccines will be an effective strategy to treat cancer.
the use of mAb to costimulate or interfere with inhibitory signals in combination with cancer vaccines is highly effective and can be safely administered to patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mAb and vaccines can be combined in a variety of ways to enhance immunity against cancer.

the immune system is a powerful weapon against cancer, and that the immune system can be guided to fight tumors by vaccines, and the immune system can also be enhanced by immunostimulatory antibodies.
the combination of a mAb that costimulates T cells with a vaccine that activates T cells and dendritic cells can be a potent combination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of cancer vaccines and immunostimulatory monoclonal antibodies has the potential to be a powerful approach for cancer immunotherapy.
